label: Outside witness
knownFor: A Roman biographer of the emperors, who notes that Claudius expelled Jews stirred up by "Chrestus" and that Nero punished the Christians.
datesNote: Born about 69 or about 77; dismissed by Hadrian about 121

keyWorks.title: Lives of the Caesars
keyWorks.about: twelve rulers from Julius Caesar to Domitian, with the notices in the lives of Claudius and Nero

remembered: John Rolfe, his translator, says Tertullian of Carthage drew on Suetonius's work about the public shows. Rolfe adds that the influence of Suetonius is seen in the form of the Life of Ambrose by Paulinus, Ambrose's secretary.

uncertain: Rolfe and the notes to Thomson and Forester's edition both read "Chrestus" as Christ. Rolfe calls it another form of Christus and thinks Suetonius probably got the date wrong, though a Jew of that name may be meant. The Thomson and Forester notes say Suetonius moved Christ to Rome and into the reign of Claudius.
Thomson and Forester translate "one Chrestus." Rolfe notes that the Latin has no word for "one" here, and takes that as a sign that Christ is meant.
The Thomson and Forester notes cite Luke, in Acts 18:2, for the expulsion of the Jews by Claudius. They add that Dio Cassius says he only forbade their meetings.
Rolfe reports two dates for his birth: 77, from Mommsen, and 69, from Macé, which Rolfe thinks somewhat more probable. The Thomson and Forester preface puts it late in the reign of Vespasian.
Suetonius blames Nero for the great fire, but his notice of the Christians does not mention it.

briefReferences: Lives of the Caesars, Claudius 25.4, Latin with English, tr. John C. Rolfe: the expulsion of the Jews at the instigation of Chrestus, set between the freedom from every burden for the people of Ilium and the German envoys allowed to sit in the orchestra.

Lives of the Caesars, Nero 16.2, tr. Rolfe: punishment of the Christians, set between the limit on cooked food in the taverns and the end of the chariot drivers' diversions. Nero 19.3: these acts are some beyond criticism. Nero 38: Nero set fire to the city.

John C. Rolfe, The Life and Works of Suetonius: the Lives of the Caesars, published in 120, twelve lives from Julius to Domitian; his intimate friendship with Pliny the Younger; secretary to Hadrian, and discharged by him.
Rolfe's note on Claudius 25.4: Chrestus another form of Christus; an error in chronology, or some Jew of that name.

Lives of the Twelve Caesars, tr. Alexander Thomson, revised by T. Forester, 1909, preface and notes 335 and 528: his closest friendship with Pliny; how little even the well-informed Suetonius knew; Chrestus a name in use among the Greeks and Romans; Christ moved from Jerusalem to Rome and into the time of Claudius; the note setting Tacitus on Nero's Christians beside Nero 16.
Acts 18:1-2, World English Bible: Paul at Corinth, and Aquila and his wife, come from Italy after Claudius commanded the Jews to leave Rome.

Tertullian, Apology 3, Latin ed. Franz Oehler, 1853, and English in the Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 3: the Romans wrongly pronounce the name Chrestianus; Oehler's note sets it beside Suetonius, Claudius 25.
Lactantius, Divine Institutes IV.7, in the Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 7: the ignorant call Christ Chrestus by the change of a letter; the editor's note on chrestos as kind, gentle, good.
Carl Mirbt, source book on the history of the papacy, 1911, and Schanz, Hosius and Krüger, history of Roman literature, 1922: both lines printed among the testimonies.

quotationOriginals.modern: He drove from Rome the Jews who were constantly rioting at the urging of Chrestus.
quotationOriginals.printed: Iudaeos impulsore Chresto assidue tumultuantis Roma expulit.
quotationOriginals.work: Suetonius, Lives of the Caesars, Claudius 25.4, Latin, with tr. John C. Rolfe (1914)
quotationOriginals.englishPrinted: Since the Jews constantly made disturbances at the instigation of Chrestus, he expelled them from Rome.
quotationOriginals.uncertain: The Latin has no word for "since", "all" or "one". Rolfe adds "since"; the Thomson and Forester English adds "all" and "one".

quotationOriginals.modern: because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome,
quotationOriginals.printed: because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome.

quotationOriginals.modern: Punishments were inflicted on the Christians, a kind of people given to a new and harmful superstition.
quotationOriginals.printed: afflicti suppliciis Christiani, genus hominum superstitionis novae ac maleficae
quotationOriginals.work: Suetonius, Lives of the Caesars, Nero 16.2, Latin, with tr. John C. Rolfe (1914)
quotationOriginals.englishPrinted: Punishment was inflicted on the Christians, a class of men given to a new and mischievous superstition.
quotationOriginals.uncertain: For maleficae Rolfe has "mischievous" and the Thomson and Forester English "impious"; their note takes the word to suggest witchcraft. The modern English says "harmful".

quotationOriginals.printed: I have brought together these acts of his, some of which are beyond criticism,
quotationOriginals.work: Suetonius, Lives of the Caesars, Nero 19.3, tr. John C. Rolfe (1914)
quotationOriginals.original: Haec partim nulla reprehensione, partim etiam non mediocri laude digna in unum contuli

quotationOriginals.printed: How little even the well-informed Suetonius knew of the real facts
quotationOriginals.work: Lives of the Twelve Caesars, tr. Alexander Thomson, revised by T. Forester (1909), note 335

quotationOriginals.modern: And even when you wrongly say 'Chrestianus', since you do not even know the name for certain, it is formed from sweetness or kindness.
quotationOriginals.printed: Yes, and even when it is wrongly pronounced by you “Chrestianus” (for you do not even know accurately the name you hate), it comes from sweetness and benignity.
quotationOriginals.work: Tertullian, Apology 3, in the Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 3
quotationOriginals.uncertain: The modern English is made from Tertullian's Latin in Franz Oehler's edition (1853). The Ante-Nicene English has "the name you hate" where the Latin says only "the name".
